q: Food security generally does not imply
options: “access by all people at all times to enough food for an active, healthy life”
“ensuring that all people at all times have both physical and economic access to basic food they need”
“the ability to assure, on a long term basis, that the food system provides the total population access to a timely, reliable and nutritionally adequate supply of food”
“Access by all people at all times, the food of their choice”
key_text: “Access by all people at all times, the food of their choice”
explanation: Food security means physical and economic access for all people at all times to sufficient, safe and nutritious food; it does not mean access to 'the food of their choice'.

notes.text: - **PDS** = distribution of essential commodities to a large number of people through a **network of Fair Price (ration) Shops at subsidised prices**; food procured by FCI goes to the poorer sections.

- **Main aim:** **food security for the poor** – to **protect the low-income / vulnerable sections against high prices** by guaranteeing a minimum quantity at affordable prices; also checks **hoarding and black-marketing** and stabilises prices ("all of the above").

q: Which of the following agency has launched Global Food Security Platform to strengthen the private sector's ability to respond to food crisis and boost food production.
explanation: The Global Food Security Platform (2022, about $6 billion) was launched by the International Finance Corporation, the World Bank Group's private-sector arm – not the World Bank itself or FAO.

notes.text: - **Global Food Security Platform** (2022, $6 billion): launched by the **International Finance Corporation (IFC)** of the World Bank Group to help the private sector respond to the food crisis.

explanation: NFSM was launched in 2007-08 in pursuance of the National Development Council resolution of 29 May 2007 on food security – the 'National Food Security Resolution' of the key; the other names are not used.
